references.text: Balak previously took Balaam to another place (the field of Zophim on the top of Pisgah) in hopes that God would permit a curse from there; this same pattern is repeated here.
This is the third time Balak takes Balaam to a new location to attempt cursing Israel, a recurring motif in the narrative.
The following verse shows that Balaam finally realized it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, in contrast to Balak's hope that God would be pleased to curse them.
Balak's frustration that Balaam blesses instead of curses reveals his persistent attempts to find a place where a curse might succeed.
Balak's final reaction shows that his repeated efforts to find a suitable place for cursing were in vain.
The question of what is right in God's eyes ('יישר בעיני') is an important theme—Balak hoped to find God's will, but on his own terms.
